title: Marshal Royal and carrying every instrument to L.A. sessions
summary: Junior was helped by Marshal Royal; session players must bring every instrument; Carmen refused to be a musician.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Another time, in talking to Ernie, he said Marshal Royal--he's a sax player, isn't he?
He said--well, like you were talking about, some years ago when you met him, he's been a lot of help to him in that his contacts.

He said he was on a session one day and Marshal was on it and Marshal was playing first alto, and of course he was on baritone, and the contractor, or whoever it was, Marshal looked at it and said, they didn't tell me to bring a piccolo and this director said I called

you for the session. While they were talking, he said, Marshal, as long as you've been coming to recording sessions, you should bring the works, bring everything, and Ernie said he looked (inaudible). He said to Marshal, do you want to use mine? He said I'd appreciate it, and he said after that, Marshal threw a lot of things his way, and he would tell the people if you call him, he'll have everything to work with.
That's typical Los Angeles. Take all the instruments because you don't know what you're going to play.

As I said, my daughter always said I've known musicians--and in school she toured with the a capello choir, the last two years at Lincoln, and a funny thing, she was dating a musician, and she has nothing against musicians, but she was determined she was not going to be a musician.
